Gingerbread Hearts

Served at: Krampusnacht

Makes about 24-30 cookiesPrep 45 min (plus 2 hours chilling)Cook 10-12 min

Gingerbread Hearts, or Lebkuchenherzen, are a beloved confection often found at Christmas markets throughout Central Europe. While Krampusnacht on December 5th is a time for mischievous spirits, these sweet, spiced cookies offer a comforting and festive treat, perfect for sharing with those who've been nice (or perhaps to appease a passing Krampus).

Ingredients

  • 2 1/4 cups (270 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 cup (120 g) unsalted butter, softened
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) honey or dark molasses
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar
  • 1 large egg
  • 1 teaspoon baking soda
  • 1 tablespoon ground ginger
  • 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cloves
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • For the Icing:
  • 2 cups (240 g) powdered sugar
  • 3-4 tablespoons (45-60 ml) lemon juice or milk
  • Optional: Food coloring for decoration

Method

  1. In a large bowl, cream together the softened butter, honey (or molasses), and granulated sugar until light and fluffy.
  2. Beat in the egg until well combined.
  3. In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, ground ginger, ground cinnamon, ground cloves, ground nutmeg, and salt.
  4. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, mixing until a soft dough forms. Do not overmix.
  5. Divide the dough in half, flatten each half into a disc, wrap tightly in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours (or overnight) to firm up.
  6. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C). Line baking sheets with parchment paper.
  7. On a lightly floured surface, roll out one disc of chilled dough to about 1/4 inch (6 mm) thickness.
  8. Using a heart-shaped cookie cutter (about 3-4 inches or 7-10 cm), cut out cookies and carefully place them on the prepared baking sheets, leaving about 1 inch (2.5 cm) between them.
  9. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until the edges are lightly browned and the cookies are firm to the touch.
  10. Let the cookies cool on the baking sheets for 5 minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely.
  11. While the cookies cool, prepare the icing: In a medium bowl, whisk together the powdered sugar and lemon juice (or milk) until smooth and of a thick, pipeable consistency. Add more liquid a teaspoon at a time if needed.
  12. Once the cookies are completely cool, decorate them with the icing. You can spread it with a knife or spoon, or pipe intricate designs using a piping bag with a small round tip.
  13. Allow the icing to set completely before storing the cookies.

Tips

  • For a chewier cookie, use dark molasses instead of honey.
  • If you plan to hang these as decorations, make a small hole at the top of each cookie with a skewer immediately after removing them from the oven.
  • Store gingerbread hearts in an airtight container at room temperature for up to two weeks; they tend to soften and improve in flavor over a day or two.
